title: Monopoly was invented to show how harmful monopolies are
description:
In 1904, Elizabeth Magie patented The Landlord's Game, a board game about how land rent makes some people rich and ruins others. Here's how a game against monopolies became the most famous game about monopoly.
#monopoly #boardgames #economics #money #shorts

scenes.narration: Monopoly was invented to warn us about monopolies.
scenes.imagePrompt: two dice rolling across a vintage board game, dramatic low light, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: Nineteen oh four. An American woman, Elizabeth Magie, gets a patent for a new board game.
scenes.imagePrompt: early 1900s patent drawing of a square board game on aged paper, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: It was called The Landlord's Game. It showed how landowners get rich off rent, while tenants go broke.
scenes.imagePrompt: row of small old houses on a street at dusk, one lit window, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: Magie wrote two sets of rules. In one, everyone won as wealth grew. In the other, one player took it all.
scenes.imagePrompt: board game pieces split into two groups on a table, contrasting light, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: People liked the second version better. The game kept getting reworked, and in thirty-five it was sold to Parker Brothers as Monopoly.
scenes.imagePrompt: 1930s toy shop shelves stacked with board game boxes, warm nostalgic light, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: The company bought Magie's patent for just five hundred dollars. No royalties on sales.
scenes.imagePrompt: a few old paper dollar bills on a wooden desk next to a fountain pen, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: The irony? A game against greed became one of the best-selling board games in the world. And now you win by bankrupting everyone else.
scenes.imagePrompt: a single game token standing on a pile of coins, everyone else knocked over, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: So, do you usually win at Monopoly? Tell me in the comments.
